Okay, first. Biological immortals - the Centurions. A group of powerful human beings who, thanks to a number of scientific innovations, cannot age. Of course, by the time the main story takes place, most of them are dead, but that's irrelevant to this question.

As for deities, there are two main godlike beings in my world - the first (though I hesitate to order them first and second) are the Sentinels of Dawn, mechanized warriors created in the early dawn of Time to protect and serve a once-great Empire. Eons after it has faded away into nonexistence, they still stand guard, waiting for the day when the heir returns to restore the Empire to its former glory.

A regulatory freeze refers to a temporary halt on the implementation or enforcement of new regulations or rules by a government or regulatory body. This can occur when a new administration takes office or when there is a need to review existing regulations. During a regulatory freeze, agencies may pause any pending regulations to assess their impact, gather public input, or reconsider their necessity. This process can affect various sectors, including environmental, financial, and health regulations, and is often aimed at reducing the regulatory burden on businesses and individuals.

I can see a conflict forming between two key characters regarding a third character. One character banished her with the full intent of having her die out there, so I imagine finding out that she's not only alive, but that the other character trusts and likely cares for her will create a huge rift between them.

I can also see conflicts arising in the underground shelter. Based on all we've seen of the local tribes in the past four seasons, I cannot see them abandoning their clan rivalries. One leader mentioned that without a strong figure, the clans wouldn't unite, and I can't see them leading well for six years on limited resources, especially for the tribal groups. The group from the sky will be fine - they've been through it all before and worse, but the tribes (from what we've seen) have never dealt with this kind of situation. Because of this, I can see the sky group acting as mediators between the clans, as they know how hard it is to live like the underground group is living, but they also know it's possible to survive it. I can see one character taking the lead in this.

I can see this conflict being amplified when the sky group and the underground group are reunited with each other and back out on the surface fighting for food and land in the tiny patch of livable land. I can also see the third character playing into this (which is part of why I think they made her a regular). She was a spy for a rival faction and is likely the highest member of their chain of command left alive. The tribes value tradition, so I can see the rival faction and their allies, if they have any, looking towards her as a leader. She can either join them or say, "I just spent six years in space, I'll pass on your conflict."

I can also, of course, see a conflict between the underground group/sky group and another faction. I think they've gone to war. A few reasons for it.

1) We don't know the size of the bunker. All we know is that it can hold at least 1200 people, but it could easily be more. The writers have a lot of wiggle room there.

2) The grounders aren't used to those conditions. They've never, from what we've seen, had to deal with rationing or cramped living quarters. Never had to deal with limited supplies like they will be.

3) The group from the sky is angry and in power. They are the only ones that know how to operate the bunker, but they're also reasonably upset because 300 of their own were killed after they had already all been safe, even if how they got to be safe was illegitimate.

4) A key character. The creator has said in interviews she'll be in a place people don't expect, but I think there were a few hints to it in her last conversation with another character. a) The girl under the floor and b) Prometheus. Both, obviously, references to the first season, but given the "reset" that the fifth season will be, I can see them being a hint of things to come for her.

5) Another character. They made her actor a regular for a reason, and I don't think it was availability concerns like was no doubt the reason another character became one. She is, at the end of the fourth season, a banished scout/spy from a rival faction. I think both of these things will come into play. Her banishment, obviously, will cause conflict with the key character and another leader. Both of them never expected her to live, so seeing her alive after 6 years and more importantly seeing her with another character and probably pretty close to him will upset them both. Likewise, her position as one of the only surviving commanders from her faction will come into play with the grounder conflict I anticipate. Her faction and their allies will likely ask her to lead them, and she either gives them the finger and goes with the other character, or she betrays him. I would obviously prefer the latter option, but I can see them pulling the former. At the very least I expect her to be conflicted no matter what choice she makes.

A few problems with that:

1) How do they acquire the AI? And furthermore, how do they even learn about it? The only reason they discovered it was because a character died and another happened to be in the room (and thus knew it was an AI).

2) What happens next season? (spoilers for Season 4) With the whole impending disaster, if she were exiled, they would have had to bring her back to the main location. The problem with this is that 1) she would have been exiled or thought dead, 2) a key character never would have worked for the protagonist without the important artifact (as he knew it contained the essence of a previous leader, which convinced him that she was serious), and 3) the writers would have had to not only deal with all of this but also somehow find a way to bring the actress back for filming. Since she'd likely have a significant role in the plot, they'd have to bring her back for most episodes or end up killing her anyway, in which case it's better for the sake of the show that she dies in Season 3, since it advanced the plot and the characters.

3) What plausible scenario could lead to her being "excommunicated"? She was one of their best fighters and the leader. Some may have grown angry with her, but most would not because it was their tradition to obey their leader.

4) How do they account for her being missing for the rest of the season and the protagonist not following her? Or the leader not following the protagonist? They both cared for each other, so I'm not really sure there's any reason for them to leave each other, nor any reason to then ignore the leader for the rest of the season.

And the biggest issue of all,

5) She'd weigh down the show for all the reasons I listed above and likely many more. Because they could probably only end up getting her for 1 or 2 episodes, they'd have to account for her absence for the entire season and come up with excuse after excuse for why she disappeared again, to the point where she is pretty much dead anyway. Then somehow they'd have to bring her back for at least the final two episodes and save her, because if they didn't, then there'd be no point in having prevented her death in the first place.

I didn't want her to die, but it had to happen. If the actress hadn't been involved in another project, then they could have kept her, but real life got in the way. Keeping her alive would just complicate things to the point where it's not worth it, because they could easily have ended up only being able to use her for one episode in Season 4.
